note: Declared deltas of the native Claude roles (ADR 0037): a Semantic Core invariant that a native role does not bind in its body on purpose. Every other invariant is evidenced in the file (tests/helpers/native-invariant-evidence.ts). A delta is stale, and fails the suite, when the role's body does evidence the invariant.

deltas.feature: Check for delivered peer messages before the final report.
deltas.rationale: Tier-1 specialists stay hub-and-spoke (maintainer decision, plan 032 close-out, kept 2026-10-04): their body forbids messaging a sibling and routes every peer question through the lead, so there is no peer inbox to check. The lead relays and wakes.

deltas.feature: The handoff report lists peer messages received and open items.
deltas.rationale: `Open items` is bound in the specialist's own body (maintainer decision, 2026-10-04, ADR 0038). `Peer messages received` is not: a hub-and-spoke Tier-1 specialist never receives a peer message, so the section would always read none; the lead's brief template still asks for it.

deltas.feature: Message a peer directly only in team mode, when the brief lists that peer.
deltas.rationale: Stricter than the invariant: a Tier-1 specialist never messages a peer (its body says so), because team mode belongs to the Tier-2 packages on Agent Teams.

deltas.feature: At most two peer exchanges per specialist pair and one directed question per peer per planning round.
deltas.rationale: Stricter than the invariant: a Tier-1 reviewer or indexer holds no peer exchange at all, so the budget is zero.

deltas.feature: Component contracts settle through the orchestrator before touching peer-owned files.
deltas.rationale: The lead owns contract-first (it hands the contract as a fixed input before the slice starts); the specialist's body routes every question for a peer through the lead but does not name peer-owned files.

deltas.feature: Consult at least one relevant specialist read-only before the delegation map, unless the user waives it.
deltas.rationale: Decided by the coordinating AI session on 2026-11-22, the maintainer's to overturn. The Prime Orchestrator on this host routes and holds no Agent tool, so it consults no specialist and builds no delegation map. ADR 0010 rejected stay-and-delegate, the Bundle ships no specialist, and a department lead run as a subagent loses its structured questions and its allowlist. The duty stays in the floor from the Semantic Core; the body says plainly that this lane neither consults nor executes in session.

deltas.feature: A slice executed in session is delegated to domain specialists: the orchestrator coordinates and reviews and does not write the implementation itself.
deltas.rationale: Decided by the coordinating AI session on 2026-11-22, the maintainer's to overturn. The Prime Orchestrator on this host executes no department work in session at all: it routes, and the department lead runs the work as the main agent of a fresh session. It holds no Agent tool to delegate with, the Bundle ships no specialist, and a department lead run as a subagent loses its structured questions and its allowlist (ADR 0010 rejected stay-and-delegate).

deltas.feature: Every delegation brief carries objective, scope, acceptance evidence, peer routing, and report format.
deltas.rationale: Decided by the coordinating AI session on 2026-11-22, the maintainer's to overturn. With no Agent tool the Prime Orchestrator issues no delegation, so there is no brief to write. The hand-off to a department lead is a handoff note and a start line (ADR 0010), not a delegation.

deltas.feature: The coordinator relays between specialists and wakes a finished peer before expecting its reply.
deltas.rationale: Decided by the coordinating AI session on 2026-11-22, the maintainer's to overturn. The Prime Orchestrator spawns no specialist, so there is no peer to relay between and none to wake. A department lead does that in its own session.
